text:
Reveille sounded in every barracks,
and the morning wind put out the lamps.

It was the hour when swarms of evil dreams
smother adolescents on their pillows;
when, like a throbbing, bloodshot eye,
the lamp makes a red stain upon the day,
and the soul, beneath the weight of the sleeping body,
imitates the struggles of daylight and lamp.
Like a tearful face wiped by the breeze,
a tremor of fleeting things fills the air,
and men tire of writing and of love.

Here and there the houses begin to smoke;
the women of pleasure, eyelids livid,
lie open-mouthed in broken sleep;
the poor women, dragging their cold, thin breasts,
blow upon the embers and their fingers.
It is the hour when, wrapped in grime and cold,
women in labor feel their pains increase;
like a broken sob amid the welling blood,
the cockcrow tears the dark air;
an ocean of mist bathes the buildings,
and the dying, inside the hospitals,
breathe their last between uneven hiccups.
The libertines return, shattered by their work.

Shivering dawn, dressed in green and rose,
advanced slowly over the deserted Seine,
and somber Paris, rubbing its eyes,
grasped its tools, an old laborer.

translation.title: Morning Twilight
translation.editorial_note: Translated from the supplied Spanish version of Baudelaire. The dawn sequence and its parallel scenes of exhaustion, labor, birth, and death are preserved.
